paragraphs: In Northamptonshire, fostering for children in care is run by Northamptonshire Children's Trust on behalf of North Northamptonshire Council and West Northamptonshire Council. Both councils point people who want to foster to the Trust, which handles enquiries, training and support for carers. Independent agencies, such as those listed on this page, also care for children from the county.

In January 2025 the Trust's fostering service manager told local radio that there are three basic requirements: being over 21, having a spare room and living permanently in the UK. He added that there is no upper age limit, with carers ranging from 21 to their late 70s. Check the current criteria with the Trust when you enquire.

Fostering Friendly support is growing locally. West Northamptonshire Council was accredited by The Fostering Network as a Fostering Friendly employer in 2023, giving staff who foster extra help to balance work and caring, and in May 2026 the Trust announced a Fostering Friendly Pledge inviting local businesses to offer foster families discounts, wellbeing support and other perks.
The pages we read do not publish allowance figures, so ask the Trust and two or three of the agencies below what they pay, what training they give and how they support carers day to day.
